=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- Requirement: "Every call keeps its unchanged codex or OpenCode command as the exit-75 fallback in the same attempt." (from PR description)
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, poller_judge_isolated
  Evidence of absence: When Claude returns exit 75 inside poller_judge_isolated, the retry calls _poller_rb_judge_sandbox_attempt with engine codex, which runs OpenCode in the isolated sandbox. The poller judges' pre-Codex command was host codex --sandbox danger-full-access, which is never invoked. The agents.md model table documents this as "isolated OpenCode fallback for poller judges" and the isolation issues #6357, #6358, #6337, #6359 explicitly prohibit host-executed judges. The PR description line was written before those isolation changes merged; the described "unchanged codex call" is intentionally superseded by the isolation requirements, and the actual behavior matches the documented intent in agents.md and the isolation changelog fragments.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: "Fetch the Claude CLI and account-pool credential 'only when a judge resolves to Claude.'" (from PR description)
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml, Resolve AI engine step
  Evidence of absence: The preflight at orchestrate_poll.yml lines 715-716 sets any_claude=true when any tracking issue carries ai:engine-claude, without checking for ai:codex on the same issue. Since ai:codex takes precedence in resolve_role, a project with both labels resolves its judges to Codex, yet the preflight still triggers a CLI install and credential fetch. Both operations are continue-on-error: true and fail-open, so correctness is not affected; the sole impact is wasted runner time and a benign API call on ticks with such a project.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- Requirement: "Every call keeps its unchanged codex or OpenCode command as the exit-75 fallback in the same attempt." (PR description, "What changes" section summary)
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh poller_judge_isolated and _poller_rb_judge_sandbox_attempt, and the WAVE_JUDGE / STALL_JUDGE / INTEGRATION_JUDGE / SECURITY_JUDGE / RB_JUDGE call sites that previously ran host codex
  Evidence of absence: The pre-Phase 5c poller judge call sites (WAVE_JUDGE in scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh before the PR, plus the four other roles) ran `codex --ask-for-approval never -c model_verbosity=low -c include_apply_patch_tool=true exec --skip-git-repo-check --model "${MODEL_EDITOR}" --sandbox danger-full-access` directly on the host. The new poller_judge_isolated wrapper routes Claude-unavailable (exit-75) through _poller_rb_judge_sandbox_attempt with engine=codex, which runs the OpenCode CLI inside the network-isolated review sandbox (review_untrusted_sandbox.sh run codex ...), not the prior host codex command. The agents.md "Models in use" row for the orchestrator judges and the test test_all_poller_judges_are_read_only_and_never_use_host_fallback in tests/test_orchestrator_judges_claude_engine.py codify the new sandbox-isolated OpenCode fallback as the intentional design. The ORCHESTRATE decomposer's exit-75 fallback (orchestrate.yml "Run Codex (decomposer)") IS the unchanged host codex call, so the PR description is correct for ORCHESTRATE but misleading for the poller judges. The new sandbox-isolated OpenCode path is a deliberate security improvement (PR-derived prompts no longer run with host credentials in reach) and matches the documented design; the PR description wording should be tightened to reflect the new fallback path for the five poller judges.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: The Claude CLI install and account-pool credential resolve steps run "only when a judge resolves to Claude" (PR description, "Poller judges" Claude engine comment in orchestrate_poll.yml)
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml Resolve AI engine step, preflight jq check (the "if jq -e 'any(.[]; any(.labels[]?; .name == \"ai:engine-claude\"))'" block within the step that the original PR diff adds starting at line 691)
  Evidence of absence: The preflight sets any_claude=true when any active tracking issue has the ai:engine-claude label, without excluding issues that also carry ai:codex. The engine resolver (scripts/claude_engine.py resolve_role) ranks ai:codex above ai:engine-claude, so an issue with both labels resolves to codex for every judge role (the CLAUDE_FIXER_ROLES branch returns codex when CLAUDE_FIXER_ENABLED=false; non-CLAUDE_FIXER_ROLES fall to the LABEL_CODEX branch). When the resolver returns codex the subsequent "Install Claude Code CLI" and "Resolve Claude credential" steps run unnecessarily. Both install steps carry continue-on-error: true and the call-site engine selection honors the labels correctly, so this is a wasted-setup efficiency concern, not a correctness defect. The fix is to either (a) gate the preflight on a label co-occurrence check that excludes ai:codex, or (b) drop the first jq check entirely because the per-role `ai_engine_for_role` loop already calls the resolver and would naturally honor the labels.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

  SEVERITY: MAJOR

- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:715-716 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The preflight sets any_claude=true when ANY tracking issue has `ai:engine-claude`, but the engine resolver gives `ai:codex` precedence. An issue with both labels triggers unnecessary Claude CLI installation and credential fetching.
  WHY: Wastes resources installing Claude and fetching credentials when the judge will use codex anyway. Does not affect correctness, only efficiency.
